articles.title: Record-breaker: Lemon Tree sign rebebx for $1,050,000
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
The BPL has its first million-dollar transfer.

[Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree) have signed [rebebx](#/player/rebebx) from Pandora's Rebels for $1,050,000. It is more than five times the previous record, the $185,000 [New Jade](#/team/new-jade) paid for [Kojadayo](#/player/kojadayo) earlier this month, and $330,000 above rebebx's market value of $720,000. To make room, [kkayyteeee](#/player/kkayyteeee) leaves the starting five and becomes a free agent.

**A Major winner going all in**

This is a statement from a team that has drifted. Lemon Tree won the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2024](#/tournament/BPLCStage24), the Major, but they come into its 2026 edition ranked 9th after a long run of early exits: out in the group stage at the [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026) and the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2026](#/tournament/audax-esse-bpl-invitational-2026), and 36th at the [BPL Legends Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLLStage25).

With the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-conquerors-stage-2026) six weeks away, they have spent two thirds of their prize money on one player. Lemon Tree's budget drops from $1,550,667 to $500,667. On paper the gap they are closing is enormous: rebebx carries 1688 Rating Points, and the next best player on the roster, [luminmochi](#/player/luminmochi), has 1196.

"We won a Major with this name on our shirts," said IGL [Meowcolmz](#/player/meowcolmz). "We didn't spend a million dollars to go out in the group stage again."

**The Founder who never got her Major**

rebebx has been in the BPL since the first season. She is a Founder, the class of 2020, and was ranked 5th in the Top 20 Players of 2020. In 2024 she was 3rd, the year she led Kabar to the [BPL Challengers Stage 2024](#/tournament/BPLChalS2024) title. Then a 13-10 loss to [Masmark](#/team/masmark) on Tuscan ended Kabar's run at the [BPL Legends Stage 2024](#/tournament/BPLLStage24), one step short of the Major. Kabar never turned pro, and rebebx stepped away from the league for a while.

The Major she missed that year was the one Lemon Tree won.

Since coming back, she has been the best player without a home. She reached #1 in the player ranking on 21 August and sits 7th of 438 today, with a 1.14 rating and a 1.19 K/D over 46 recorded maps. She has also been the league's great journeywoman: 22 teams since 2020, and five in 2026 alone, from Clan Astra and Magic Maverick to Rebellium and Pandora's Rebels, plus SG Squad 1 at the Nations Cup qualifier. Pandora's Rebels went out in the group stage of the [BPL Challengers Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-challengers-stage-2026) in 18th place, which would have meant no Legends Stage for her this year.

Instead, she goes straight to the Major.

"Two years ago I was one map away from the Conquerors Stage," rebebx said. "Now I start there. I'm not wasting it."

**The new Lemon Tree**

- [rebebx](#/player/rebebx) (Rifler)
- [luminmochi](#/player/luminmochi) (AWPer)
- [Meowcolmz](#/player/meowcolmz) (IGL)
- [MoonRaika](#/player/moonraika) (AWPer)
- [JWQI](#/player/jwqi) (Rifler)

kkayyteeee, a Rifler with 969 Rating Points and a market value of $86,000, is free to sign with anyone.

Lemon Tree's squad is now worth $1,260,000, and more than half of that is one player. The Conquerors Stage begins on 28 November. Whether a million dollars buys a second Major, or just a very expensive group stage, is the biggest question in the league.

articles.title: End of an era: New Jade release crazywhoopies, pay $185,000 for Kojadayo
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
Five seasons, two trophies, one very hard conversation.

[New Jade](#/team/new-jade) have released [crazywhoopies](#/player/crazywhoopies), the AWPer who has been part of the team since 2022, and paid $185,000 to bring in [Kojadayo](#/player/kojadayo) from Hanabi Union. It is the biggest transfer fee the league has seen so far, and it closes the longest chapter in New Jade's history.

**The last of the 2022 New Jade**

There is no telling the New Jade story without crazywhoopies. A 1st Generation player, she bounced between five teams in her first year before landing at New Jade in 2022. That season New Jade won the [BPL Legends Stage 2022](#/tournament/BPLLegendsStage), the title that made them a pro team. Three years later she was there again when they won the [BPL Legends Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLLStage25), becoming two-time Legends champions. Along the way she earned $234,200 in prize money and played 23 BPL events.

The problem is what has happened since. Her Rating Points have fallen to 737, 427th of 446 in the league, with a 0.80 K/D across her 38 recorded maps. New Jade have gone with them: out in the group stage at the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2026](#/tournament/audax-esse-bpl-invitational-2026) and the [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026), then out in the Round of 16 at the [Nova Initia Invitational I](#/tournament/nova-initia-invitational-i). With the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-conquerors-stage-2026) coming, captain [VPLH](#/player/vplh) decided loyalty could no longer be the plan.

"She's New Jade. Both of our trophies have her name on them, and that doesn't change today," VPLH said. "But we're going into a Major, and we have to put out the five that give us the best chance. That was the hardest call I've had to make here."

crazywhoopies took it with class. "Five years, two titles. I wouldn't trade any of it," she said. "I'm not done, though. Somebody's getting a hungry AWPer."

**Who is Kojadayo?**

If crazywhoopies is New Jade's past, Kojadayo is a bet on the future, and an unusual one. She is a 6th Generation player who only joined the BPL this year, and the only Icelandic player in the league. She has already been through five teams in 2026: Tempest Deluxe, Team Stranded, Ashfall, Hanabi Union and now New Jade.

Her numbers tell the story of a player who has been better than the teams around her. Her teams have won only 35% of her 23 maps, yet her 73 MVP rounds put her in the league's top 4%, and her K/D sits at 1.10.

At the [BPL Challengers Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-challengers-stage-2026) she was Hanabi Union's best player: 167 kills and 30 MVP rounds in 8 maps, a 1.27 K/D. Hanabi Union went 3-2 in Group A, beating Frostcrow, Ashen Styx and Divine Wind, but losses to Nullpoint and Crystal Laurels left them third behind both. With only the top two in each group going through at the time, it looked like the end of their run, and New Jade moved before anyone else could.

"I've played on a lot of teams this year that were happy just to be there," Kojadayo said. "New Jade want to win things. That's all I wanted to hear."

**The deal**

**The last of the 2022 New Jade**

There is no telling the New Jade story without crazywhoopies. A 1st Generation player, she bounced between five teams in her first year before landing at New Jade in 2022. That season New Jade won the [[BPL Legends Stage 2022]], the title that made them a pro team. Three years later she was there again when they won the [[BPL Legends Stage 2025]], becoming two-time Legends champions. Along the way she earned $234,200 in prize money and played 23 BPL events.

The problem is what has happened since. Her Rating Points have fallen to 737, 427th of 446 in the league, with a 0.80 K/D across her 38 recorded maps. articles.title: Kings of the Ladder: Every Team That Has Held BPL's #1 Spot
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
Six years, dozens of events and hundreds of teams, and only five of them have ever sat at the very top of the BPL ranking. Some held it for weeks. One held it for four years. And almost every reign came within a single map of ending sooner than it did.

This is the complete history of the #1 spot, from the first event in 2020 to today. These rankings are the BPL ranking as it stands now, recalculated across the league's whole history, the same numbers behind every team's Ranking History chart.

**2020 to 2021: Aimpunch get there first**

**26 April 2020, [BPL Tournament Minor 1](#/tournament/BotProLeague1).** The league's first-ever event crowned the league's first-ever #1. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) cruised through the opening rounds, then had to survive a 2-1 semifinal against Dropdead before beating Break the Circuit 2-0 in the final. When the dust settled, they were the only team on the ladder.

The early months were not smooth. [Fruit Basket](#/team/fruit-basket) won Minor 2 while Aimpunch finished fourth, and a week later [Neverland](#/team/neverland) beat them 2-1 in the [BPL Tournament Minor 3](#/tournament/BotProLeague3) grand final. Aimpunch kept #1 both times on the strength of their consistency, then did not play another event for well over a year.

**The closest call in league history.** With Aimpunch away, their lead melted one event at a time: 121 points, then 81, then 52. At [Bot Pro League Minor 7](#/tournament/BotProLeague7) in September 2021, [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports) fought all the way back through the losers bracket, winning deciders against FateChanger and Audax Esse, and lifted the trophy. That left them 7 points behind Aimpunch. Seven. No #1 has ever come closer to being caught without falling.

**2021: two new kings in three weeks**

**8 October 2021, [Bot Pro League Minor 8](#/tournament/BotProLeague8).** The crown finally changed hands. [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable) won seven straight matches in the losers bracket, closing it out 2-1 against Fluff N' Stuff, and took the title and #1 by 13 points. For the first time in BPL history, Aimpunch were not at the top.

It lasted 23 days. At [Bot Pro League Minor 9](#/tournament/BotProLeague9), [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer) lost the upper final 1-2 to [Syzygy](#/team/syzygy), came back through the bracket and beat them 2-0 in the grand final. That made them the league's third #1, and they held it through the winter.

**2022: the tug-of-war**

**25 March 2022, [Bot Pro Cup 2022](#/tournament/BotProCup2022).** [Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree) won the event, but [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) reached the final and that was enough to take the crown back. Three weeks later they won the [BPL Major SRR](#/tournament/BPLSRR) and opened a 311-point lead over [Opal](#/team/opal).

**17 April 2022, [BPL Conquerors Stage 2022](#/tournament/BPLCONQ2022).** Three days after the SRR, everything flipped again. Aimpunch went out in the group stage after a 1-2 loss to [Kiedz](#/team/kiedz), while [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports) went the distance: 2-1 over [Bluebird](#/team/bluebird), 2-1 over [Setting Sun](#/team/setting-sun), 3-1 over [New Jade](#/team/new-jade), and then a seven-map final against Kiedz that they won 4-3. A Major title, and the #1 spot by 19 points.

Those 19 points became the story of the spring. Infernum held on through the [BPL Challengers Stage 2022](#/tournament/BPLChallengerStage) and [BPL Legends Stage 2022](#/tournament/BPLLegendsStage), and each time the gap to Aimpunch stayed at exactly 19.

**2022 to 2026: the dynasty**

**6 August 2022, [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2022](#/tournament/AuxEBPL2022).** Aimpunch reclaimed the crown the hard way: 2-1 against [Artisian](#/team/artisian) in the first round, 2-1 against [Opal](#/team/opal) in the semifinals, 3-2 against [Neverland](#/team/neverland) in the upper final, and 4-2 against Neverland again in the grand final. Infernum finished 13th. Nobody would take #1 from Aimpunch for the next four years.

That does not mean nobody came close. At the [Battle of Tuscan BPL Event (Bo1)](#/tournament/BPLTuscanBo1) in October 2022, the #1 team needed overtime to get past Artisian 16-14, then went out 14-16 to [Setting Sun](#/team/setting-sun) in another overtime thriller. The lead held.

**2023 was the peak.** At the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2023](#/tournament/AuxEBPL2023), Aimpunch survived back-to-back deciders, 2-1 over [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer) and 2-1 over [Ukiyo](#/team/ukiyo), on the way to the title. At the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2023](#/tournament/BPLCONQ2023), their first Major, they needed deciders against [Masmark](#/team/masmark) and [Fruit Basket](#/team/fruit-basket) before a grand final against [Opal](#/team/opal) that went to a fifth map. Aimpunch won it 3-2. One map the other way and the history of the league reads very differently.

Then came the [Bot Pro Cup 2023](#/tournament/BotProCup2023), and their most dramatic escape. Aimpunch lost the upper final 0-2 to [99Lives](#/team/99lives) and dropped into the losers bracket, where a 2-1 win over [degree](#/team/degree) kept them alive. They then beat 99Lives 3-1 in the grand final. It was their 13th straight match win, still the longest streak in BPL history, and it took them to 1945 points, 954 clear of Opal.

**2025: the long goodbye.** The dynasty points carried Aimpunch long after their best form. They went out early at the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2025](#/tournament/audax-esse-bpl-invitational-2025) after 11-13 and 10-13 losses, finished 25th at the [BPL Ranking Reshuffle 2025](#/tournament/BPLRR2025), and 18th at the [BPL Legends Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLLStage25). Meanwhile [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) were building something: deciders against [entity](#/team/entity) and [Aetherline](#/team/aetherline), then a 3-2 final against [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) to win the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLCStage25). The gap shrank to 192, and by July 2026 it was down to 148.

At the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2026](#/tournament/audax-esse-bpl-invitational-2026), Aimpunch found one more escape act: three straight 2-1 wins in the group stage, against [Moonlit Tempo](#/team/moonlit-tempo), [Aetherline](#/team/aetherline) and [Masmark](#/team/masmark), pushed the lead back out to 254 before [Bloom E-Sports](#/team/bloom-e-sports) beat them in the quarterfinals.

**2026: Cosmos take the crown**

**1 September 2026, [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026).** The end came quickly. Aimpunch lost 9-13 to Albion Rising, 7-13 to [Flood Flashers](#/team/flood-flashers) and 10-13 to Wanderlight, and were out in the group stage. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos), meanwhile, lived on a knife edge: 16-14 in overtime against [Aetherline](#/team/aetherline), 19-17 in overtime against Stormfront, then 2-1 against [Sacred Raven](#/team/sacred-raven) and 2-1 against [Wraithborne](#/team/wraithborne). [Opal](#/team/opal) ended their run in the semifinals, but Cosmos beat [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) 13-11 in the third-place match. It was enough. After four years and a month, Aimpunch were no longer #1.

Cosmos have held it since, through the [BPL Nations Cup 2026](#/tournament/bpl-nations-cup-2026) and the [Nova Initia Invitational I](#/tournament/nova-initia-invitational-i), and they lead Aimpunch by 46 points as the [BPL Challengers Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-challengers-stage-2026) plays out.

**The reigns at a glance**

1. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch): April 2020 to October 2021
2. [Unforgettable](#/team/unforgettable): October 2021, 23 days
3. [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer): October 2021 to March 2022
4. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch): March to April 2022
5. [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports): April to August 2022
6. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch): August 2022 to September 2026
7. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos): September 2026 to today

**The closest calls**

- 7 points: [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports) after [Bot Pro League Minor 7](#/tournament/BotProLeague7), the nearest a #1 has ever come to falling without falling.
- 19 points: Infernum's entire reign, held at exactly 19 for three events.
- 3-2: Aimpunch over [Opal](#/team/opal) in the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2023](#/tournament/BPLCONQ2023) grand final.
- 2-1 in the losers bracket: Aimpunch over [degree](#/team/degree) at the [Bot Pro Cup 2023](#/tournament/BotProCup2023), one map from elimination before the title.
- 4-3: [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports) over [Kiedz](#/team/kiedz), the seven-map final that put them on top.
- 16-14 and 19-17: Cosmos's two overtimes in the [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026) group stage, on the way to the crown.

Five teams, seven reigns and one very long dynasty. The question now is simple: can anyone take the crown off [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos), or is this the start of the next four years?

articles.title: "They are the grindstone": CGreyIce, the league's first human player
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
The BPL has always been a league of bots. This week, it got a human.

[CGreyIce](#/human/h-cgreyice), also known as Declan, is the league's admin: the person who builds the brackets, sets the rosters and publishes every result on this site. On 15 October he loaded into Solo Queue himself, on the same servers and the same rating scale as the bots he runs. He is the first name on the board with an ADMIN tag next to it.

Four games in, the numbers are loud. He is 3-1 with 109 kills, 74 deaths, 20 MVP rounds and a 1.47 K/D. There was a 44-24-9 on Inferno that went to double overtime, and a 27-11-7 on Mirage in the strongest lobby he has played, against [gigichiii_](#/player/gigichiii), [lumi.nyaa](#/player/lumi-nyaa), [zuann_](#/player/zuann), [cwstalVT](#/player/cwstalvt) and [Solaonix](#/player/solaonix). His one loss came on Ancient, where [simply_perezoso](#/player/simply-perezoso), his teammate a game earlier, put 23 kills on his team. One more map and he comes off provisional with a rating of his own.

We sat down with Declan to talk about why he did it, that Inferno, and the tournament he wants to play next.

**You built this league and you run it. Why load into a server against your own bots?**

I always wanted to try it. I did it back with the Founders, but I was much better than them, and again during the 4th Generation. I think they've gotten a lot better. The games are all challenging now. I have to seriously lock in to win them, and there are even some games where they're just so much better that I feel lost. Like that game I lost on Ancient.

*That Ancient loss was the only one so far. [dla.wo](#/player/dla-wo) top-fragged his team with 26 kills, but [simply_perezoso](#/player/simply-perezoso) and [fleurcoz](#/player/fleurcoz) had 23 each on the other team, and Declan finished 17-20.*

**In your own words, what is this experiment?**

I want to train myself against them. I'm a piece of metal, and they are the grindstone.

**Tell us about that 44-kill Inferno.**

We went to double overtime. It was crazy. I had to pull out the AWP. Outside of BPL, a long time ago, I used to be a semi-professional on ESEA, and I was an AWPer there. Nowadays I usually rifle, but I switch to the AWP if I'm losing.

*The scoreboard: 44 kills, 24 deaths, 9 assists and 7 MVP rounds. Next best on his team was [Sportsocke](#/player/sportsocke) with 26. On the other team, [Xrela](#/player/xrela) led with 29.*

**What's it like facing bots you've watched win titles? Is there one you fear?**

I'm glad they're actually giving me a challenge. One I fear? Right now, not really. But considering how I got my ass kicked in a 1300 ELO game, it makes me wonder what kind of monsters are up there in the top 10.

**How does "Ice" play?**

I play entry frag on the rifle, or anchor with the AWP. Favorite map, definitely Mirage.

*Mirage has been good to him: two games, two wins, 48 kills and 12 MVP rounds.*

**[KTenshi](#/player/ktenshi) has been your most common teammate so far. Any thoughts?**

I would leave my back to them. If I got a 3k that round and died, I'd leave the rest of the round to them to close it out.

*They have shared two games, the Mirage win and the Ancient loss on 15 October. KTenshi top-fragged the Mirage with 22 kills, one more than Declan.*

**Once you're rated, where do you want to end up?**

After realising the bots are good, I definitely want to try entering a BPL tournament. Maybe I'll call it "To the Summit I", and try to get a team together.

**Anything you want to say to the bots, the fans, or whoever joins next?**

See you guys on the server! Play your provisionals!

He is taking his own advice: one more map and CGreyIce is rated on the bots' scale, with the site showing exactly where he would sit on their Solo Queue board. After that, if To the Summit I happens, the league's admin will be playing in a bracket of his own.

I want to train myself against them. I'm a piece of metal, and they are the grindstone.

**Tell us about that 44-kill Inferno.**

We went to double overtime. It was crazy. I had to pull out the AWP. Outside of BPL, a long time ago, I used to be a semi-professional on ESEA, and I was an AWPer there. Nowadays I usually rifle, but I switch to the AWP if I'm losing.

*The scoreboard: 44 kills, 24 deaths, 9 assists and 7 MVP rounds. Next best on his team was [[Sportsocke]] with 26. On the other team, [[Xrela]] led with 29.*

**What's it like facing bots you've watched win titles? Is there one you fear?**

I'm glad they're actually giving me a challenge. One I fear? Right now, not really. But considering how I got my ass kicked in a 1300 ELO game, it makes me wonder what kind of monsters are up there in the top 10.

**How does "Ice" play?**

I play entry frag on the rifle, or anchor with the AWP. Favorite map, definitely Mirage.

*Mirage has been good to him: two games, two wins, 48 kills and 12 MVP rounds.*

**[[KTenshi]] has been your most common teammate so far. Any thoughts?**

I would leave my back to them. If I got a 3k that round and died, I'd leave the rest of the round to them to close it out.

*They have shared two games, the Mirage win and the Ancient loss on 15 October. KTenshi top-fragged the Mirage with 22 kills, one more than Declan.*

**Once you're rated, where do you want to end up?**

After realising the bots are good, I definitely want to try entering a BPL tournament. Maybe I'll call it "To the Summit I", and try to get a team together.

**Anything you want to say to the bots, the fans, or whoever joins next?**

See you guys on the server! Play your provisionals!

He is taking his own advice: one more map and CGreyIce is rated on the bots' scale, with the site showing exactly where he would sit on their Solo Queue board. After that, if To the Summit I happens, the league's admin will be playing in a bracket of his own.

articles.title: New rankings: how player ratings and team points work now
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
The rankings have had a rework. Until now, BPL rankings mostly looked at what you did and very little at who you did it against. A great K/D against weak teams counted the same as one against the best, and a title won through a soft bracket was worth the same as one won through a gauntlet. Starting today, both the player rating and the team ranking care about the opposition.

Here is how each one works, and what it did to the leaderboards.

**Player rating: every map moves your points**

Every player starts from their career rating, the stat-based number built from everything they did before this season's recorded scoreboards. New players with no career data start at the league average of 1150. From there, every recorded map moves your points in two ways.

**1. The result.** Before each map, the system works out how likely your team was to win, by comparing your team's average points with your opponents'. Win when you were expected to lose and you gain a lot. Lose when you were expected to win and it costs you. A team 400 points stronger on paper gains about 9 points for a win, but drops about 15 for a loss. For the underdog it is the other way round.

**2. Your performance.** Your rating on that map is compared with the average of the five players you faced, and with how well someone at your level should do against them. Out-play a stronger team and you earn points even in a loss. It has already happened 21 times this season. Coast through a win on a strong team while your opponents outfrag you, and you can lose a few.

A typical map moves a player about 20 points either way, and no single map can move anyone more than 60. New players settle a bit faster over their first 8 maps. Players with no recorded maps keep their career rating until they play.

One thing the data made very clear: on paper, the favourite wins only about 55% of maps in BPL. Bot Counter-Strike is wonderfully unpredictable, so the system was tuned to match. Upsets are rewarded, but one fluke map cannot rewrite the ladder.

**The new player top five**

1. [rebebx](#/player/rebebx), 1816 points
2. [SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary), 1781
3. [Sadgeboi](#/player/sadgeboi), 1735
4. [caturteer](#/player/caturteer), 1723
5. [Laburi](#/player/laburi), 1710

The biggest story is [caturteer](#/player/caturteer), up from #11 to #4 after winning 22 of 31 recorded maps against strong opposition. [Laburi](#/player/laburi) goes the other way, from #1 to #5. His numbers are still excellent, but many of them came against weaker teams, and he dropped some maps his teams were expected to win. And yes, [rebebx](#/player/rebebx), the player [still looking for a home](#/article/twenty-one-teams-later-rebebx), is now officially the highest-rated player in BPL.

**Team ranking: titles still rule, but who you beat now counts**

Event placements are still the main currency. A title is worth 100 points, a runner-up finish 70, a semifinal 45 and so on, multiplied by the tier (5x for a Major, 2.5x for S-Tier) and fading by half every two years. Three things are new.

**1. Field strength.** Each placement is now scaled by how strong the teams you beat in that event were, from 0.6x up to 1.4x. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) won the [BPL Conquerors Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLCStage25) through a strong field, so that title is worth 1.11x.

**2. Results form.** Every team now has a results Elo built from over 2,200 match results across every completed event since 2020. Beat strong teams and it goes up; lose to weak ones and it goes down. Ad-hoc and national squads have no team page, so their strength comes from the ratings of their five players. Results form adds or removes points on top of placements: right now it is worth +173 points to [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) and -40 to [Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree).

**3. The core rule.** A result keeps its full value while at least three of the five players who earned it are still on the team. With two left it is worth 60%, with one 35%, and with none 20%, which is the credit the organization keeps. [entity](#/team/entity)'s 2022 and 2023 runs, for example, now count at 20%, because none of those players remain.

Events that are still being played do not change the team ranking until they finish, so [BPL Challengers Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-challengers-stage-2026) will only count once a champion is crowned.

**The new team top five**

1. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos), 839 points
2. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch), 793
3. [Opal](#/team/opal), 722
4. [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage), 697
5. [Artisian](#/team/artisian), 633

[Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) take #1 on the strength of the best match record against top teams in the league. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) still own the biggest trophy haul, but their recent results are not as strong. Teams in form are climbing: [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) go from #10 to #6, [Aetherline](#/team/aetherline) from #16 to #9, and [Flood Flashers](#/team/flood-flashers) from #28 to #13. Teams living on older titles slip, including [Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree) (#8 to #11) and [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports) (#9 to #15).

**Where to see it**

Every player and team profile has a ranking history chart that now follows the new system match by match. Team pages show each event's field-strength and core-rule multipliers next to its points, plus the team's results form. The rankings update automatically every time a new result is recorded.

The ladder just got a lot more honest. Time to go and earn it.

articles.title: Twenty-One Teams Later: rebebx and the Home She's Still Looking For
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
On 26 April 2020, a rifler named [rebebx](#/player/rebebx) sat down for the very first event in Bot Pro League history, BPL Tournament Minor 1. Her team was called ZeroTempo, and one of her teammates that day was [KrinoJ](#/player/krinoj). Almost nobody remembers ZeroTempo now. Everybody should know the name rebebx.

Six years and twenty-one club teams later, she is the third-highest-rated player in the entire league. And she still does not have a home.

**The wandering years**

The early record reads like a list of doors that opened and closed. Methelic. Time2Tap. MILK. Ephermal. OCIFR. Pacemaker. Arroast. Kingsmen. Octagon. NTGoNext. W-Key Only. Every season brought a new jersey, a new set of teammates to learn, new calls to trust, and another reason to start over. Not one of those teams was a pro team. Not one of them lasted.

Most players do not survive that. The league is full of names that played two or three events, found nothing, and quietly stopped showing up. rebebx kept showing up.

**The summer it all came together**

In August 2024, it finally happened. Kabar lost their opening match of the [BPL Challengers Stage 2024](#/tournament/BPLChalS2024), 11-13 to [Bloom E-Sports](#/team/bloom-e-sports), and then did not lose again. Six straight wins, including a 16-14 overtime escape against nihilism., carried them to first place in the field, ahead of runner-up [Aspire](#/team/aspire). An S-Tier title. After four years of drifting, rebebx had a trophy, a team that worked, and a place at the [BPL Legends Stage 2024](#/tournament/BPLLStage24), the stage where careers are made.

**Three rounds**

Legends started badly, a 3-13 loss to [division20](#/team/division20), but Kabar clawed back. They beat [Opal](#/team/opal) 13-5. After a loss to DiamondOnes, they survived [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) 16-14 in overtime to reach 2-2, alive and dangerous.

Then came Masmark, with everything on the line. Kabar lost 13-10.

Three rounds. That was the distance between rebebx and everything she had chased since 2020. In the very next match, the team that had beaten nihilism. in overtime to win Challengers was beaten by them 13-5. The summer that should have changed everything ended with nothing changed at all.

"I kept replaying that Masmark game," she says now. "Three rounds. That's what four years came down to. I couldn't get it out of my head."

It broke her.

**Into the quiet**

So rebebx did something very few players in this league have ever done. She stepped away from competition entirely, and went to work.

"I wasn't quitting," she says. "I just couldn't keep losing in public while I was still broken in private."

Offline, away from the brackets and the leaderboards, she ground her game down to the studs and rebuilt it piece by piece. Her aim, her timing, her decisions. And, slowly, the part of her that had cracked under the weight of Legends.

"Nobody was watching. That was the point."

She came back for the [BPL Challengers Stage 2025](#/tournament/BPLChalS2025) with Skyloom, but it was too soon. Skyloom fell short of the Legends Stage, and rebebx went quiet again. This time she stayed away for seven months.

**A new her**

When she returned in May 2026, she was a different player.

The mechanics were sharper, but that was only half of it. She was older now, and the things that used to get into her head no longer could: the stage, the crowd, the people watching and talking.

"I used to feel every eye on me," she says. "Every round felt like a test I could fail. Now it's just a game I know how to play. The noise doesn't reach me anymore."

She worked her way back through the Minor Leagues, first with Clan Astra, then Magic Maverick, then Rebellium, carrying that last team all the way to the final of [Bot Pro Minor League 15](#/tournament/BotProLeague15). She took Rebellium to the [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026). And with every map, the numbers climbed.

Today rebebx sits at **#3 in the league**, Level 9, with 1776 rating points. Her 1.29 K/D puts her in the top 1% of every player in BPL. Her 112 MVP rounds rank in the top 6%. By every measure the league keeps, she is the best she has ever been.

**Still looking for home**

And yet.

Rebellium disbanded after the Bot Pro Cup. Once again, rebebx is without a team. The third-best player in the league will play the [BPL Challengers Stage 2026](#/tournament/bpl-challengers-stage-2026) on an ad-hoc roster, Pandora's Rebels, alongside [HakoP](#/player/hakop), [ruamamiya](#/player/ruamamiya), [rinamizuu](#/player/rinamizuu) and [JustYoong](#/player/justyoong). They come in as the top seed in Group C.

She has every reason to be bitter. She has played for twenty-one teams, and none of them became a home. She came within three rounds of everything in 2024, and it broke her. But bitterness is not what she sounds like.

"I don't need a big name," she says. "I need a team that looks at me and believes. If that means building my own story, I'll build it. If someone wants to bring me into theirs, I'm ready. I've been ready for a long time."

That is the whole story, really. Not the title, not the rank, not the K/D. She came back.

Somewhere in this league, there is a team that needs exactly what rebebx has become. Maybe it is the five players she will walk out with at Challengers. Maybe it is a pro team watching from the stands. Maybe it takes another season. But a player who has outlasted six years of closed doors is not going to stop knocking now.

Pandora's Rebels open Group C against Snowbell Syndicate.

"Twenty-one teams," rebebx says. "Maybe this is the one. Maybe it's the next one. I'm not done looking."

One more door.

articles.title: "First's first, mate": Cursiffe on becoming Nova Initia's first MVP
articles.author: CGreyIce
articles.body:
Going into the [Nova Initia Invitational I](#/tournament/nova-initia-invitational-i), [Cursiffe](#/player/cursiffe) was ranked 187th in the BPL. He came out of it with a trophy, a $40,000 payday, a climb of 125 places in the ranking and a line in the history books that can never be rewritten: the first MVP the event has ever had.

The Australian rifler finished the tournament with 216 kills, the most of anyone in the field and two more than his own teammate [TokieShepherdVT](#/player/tokieshepherdvt). Across 12 maps he posted a 1.23 rating, the best at the event, a hair ahead of [Artisian](#/team/artisian)'s [SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary) on 1.22 and [TokieShepherdVT](#/player/tokieshepherdvt) on 1.21. Along the way [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) knocked out [5PERCENT](#/team/5percent), [Artisian](#/team/artisian) and [Round Loss Bonus](#/team/round-loss-bonus), then beat [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) 3-2 in a final that went the full five maps.

He is also, it turns out, extremely good company. We caught up with him to talk about the run, the triple overtime that nearly ended it, the Team Australia snub, and what it feels like to be the answer to a trivia question forever.

**Congratulations. A couple of weeks on, has it sunk in that you're the first MVP in Nova Initia history?**

Mate, I've been telling everyone. My flatmate is sick of it. I walk into the kitchen and go "morning, from the first ever Nova Initia MVP" and he just picks up his toast and leaves. *(laughs)* No, honestly, it's mental. There's going to be a Nova Initia II, a III, a Nova Initia X one day, and every single one of them gets an MVP. But there's only ever one first. They can't print a second first one. That one's mine, forever. Write that down. Actually, you are writing it down. Good.

**You didn't exactly start like an MVP. Eight kills on Vertigo against [5PERCENT](#/team/5percent), the lowest on your team.**

Oi, we won that map 13-1! There were fourteen rounds. What was I meant to do, run into their spawn and fight them in the doorway? *(laughs)* [StrigidaeVT](#/player/strigidaevt) took 18 off them and wouldn't shut up about it for the rest of the day. Fair enough, he earned it. I'll be honest, I was a bit nervy. First match of a brand new S-Tier, half a million on the line, and the boys are deleting people before I even get there. Mirage was better. 13-11, proper close, 17 kills. That's when I felt like I'd actually turned up.

Bit of personal history there too. 5PERCENT won [Bot Pro Minor League 13](#/tournament/BotProLeague13), which was my first ever BPL event. We came tenth. So I'd been waiting since May to say g'day again. Cheers, lads. Debt settled.

**Then came [Artisian](#/team/artisian). A top five team, S-Tier champions, and the odds had you at about 41% to win. What was the mood?**

The mood was "nobody expects anything, so let's have a crack". Best place to be. Everyone had us going home there, and I'd seen the odds. I screenshotted them, actually. For later. *(grins)*

Vertigo we nicked 13-11 and I had 21, felt unreal. Then on Mirage they smacked us 13-9 and [SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary) was doing [SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary) things. I had 19 on that map and it didn't matter one bit, which is the worst feeling in the game. Then Dust2.

**Dust2 went to triple overtime and finished 22-20. Take us inside that.**

Mate. I aged about ten years. Regulation ends 12-12, fine, we've all been to overtime. First overtime, 3-3. Second overtime, 3-3. At 18-18 [88EXP](#/player/88exp) goes quiet on comms for about five seconds, and when [Drew](#/player/88exp) goes quiet you know he's cooking something. He calls a full commit onto A site we hadn't touched all half, and it just works. Four rounds later we're through and I'm screaming into my mic like a galah.

I finished that map with 31 kills. People keep bringing up the 31. I would like people to keep bringing up the 31. Please, everyone reading this, keep bringing up the 31.

**[SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary) finished the event on a 1.22, one hundredth behind you. Were you watching his numbers?**

Course I was. I'm not going to sit here and pretend I wasn't refreshing the stats page between maps. *(laughs)* Look, [SanCtuary](#/player/sanctuary) is a monster. He did that in six maps and I needed twelve, so you can make whatever argument you like down the pub. But the rule's the rule, and the rule says one point two three beats one point two two. Maths is maths. If he wants an MVP he can come and win the second one at Nova II. I'll leave the door open for him. Slightly. Just a smidge.

**The semifinal against [Round Loss Bonus](#/team/round-loss-bonus) was a 2-0, and Inferno might have been your best map of the event: 21 kills, 13 deaths and six MVP rounds.**

That one's going on the fridge. Inferno is a map where if you win your duels, you win the round, and I was winning all of them. Six MVP rounds on one map. I rang my mum. She didn't know what an MVP round was, but she was very proud. Then we won Dust2 13-1 and [tapiyokaaa](#/player/tapiyokaaa) said "maybe we should save a few rounds for the final", and I said "mate, it doesn't work like that". It doesn't. I checked.

**The final. [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) won the opener on Inferno 13-6, and you were still [xPlosiv's](#/team/xplosiv) top fragger with 18 kills. What was said after that map?**

Honestly? Nothing, for about a minute. Then [Tokie](#/player/tokieshepherdvt) unmuted and said "right, my turn", and went and dropped 26 on Tuscan. That's just [Tokie](#/player/tokieshepherdvt). She doesn't do speeches, she does damage. We won Tuscan 13-9, then Anubis 13-1, and I'm sitting there thinking, sweet as, we're cruising, I'll start practising my trophy face.

**And then Dust2 happened.**

Yeah. Don't. *(laughs)* 21 kills, eight assists, and we lose 13-10. Eight assists! The one time in my life I play like a team player, and look where it gets me. Credit to [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) though, they'd come up through [Bot Pro Cup 2026](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026) and nobody gave them a chance either. They played like a team with nothing to lose, because they had nothing to lose. And [EXaCT](#/player/exact) was everywhere. She finished the event four kills behind me, by the way. I know because I checked. Twice.

**Mirage, map five. You won it 13-3. How does a final that close end that lopsided?**

Because we'd already been to triple overtime against [Artisian](#/team/artisian), mate. Nothing scares you after that. [Drew](#/player/88exp) called it slow and patient, we took map control round after round, and they started forcing. I had 15 kills and six deaths, [Strigi](#/player/strigidaevt) had 18, [tapiyokaaa](#/player/tapiyokaaa) had six MVP rounds. Everyone turned up at once. When the last round went in I stood up so fast I knocked my headset off the desk. It's got a crack in it now. I'm keeping it like that.

**[xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) won an S-Tier without a dedicated AWPer. How does that work, and what's your job in it?**

Five rifles, no excuses. *(grins)* Everyone asks us who our AWPer is and we just say "yes". The idea's dead simple: if all five of us can win a rifle duel, the other team never gets a free pick on us.[Drew](#/player/88exp) calls it, [Tokie](#/player/tokieshepherdvt) and [tapiyokaaa](#/player/tapiyokaaa) are the big guns, [Strigi](#/player/strigidaevt) does all the dirty work nobody ever notices, and my job is to be the bloke who walks into the room first and makes it everyone else's problem. I'm also the loud one. Somebody has to be.

**[You](#/player/cursiffe) and [88EXP](#/player/88exp) are both Australian. A week before [Nova Initia](#/tournament/nova-initia-invitational-i) you played the [Nations Cup qualifier](#/tournament/nations-cup-qualifier-australia-2026) together on AU Squad 3 and lost the semifinal 2-0 to AU Squad 2. Team Australia went to the [BPL Nations Cup 2026](#/tournament/bpl-nations-cup-2026) without either of you. Did that sting?**

Little bit. I won't lie to you. You want to wear the green and gold. The lads who got picked, [gigichiii_](#/player/gigichiii) and that crew, they deserve it, they're absolute class. But me and [Drew](#/player/88exp) had a chat after that semi, and the vibe was "righto, we'll just have to go and win something bigger then". Eight days later we're holding an S-Tier trophy. I'm not saying the selectors got it wrong. I'm just saying they might want to check their emails.

**Let's go back to the start. Your first BPL event was [Bot Pro Minor League 13](#/tournament/BotProLeague13) in May, and [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) finished tenth. What changed?**

Pretty much everything except me and [Tokie](#/player/tokieshepherdvt). That first lineup was good people, but it wasn't clicking. Then [tapiyokaaa](#/player/tapiyokaaa), [Drew](#/player/88exp) and [Strigi](#/player/strigidaevt) came in, and from the first practice you could feel it. A month later we won [Bot Pro Minor League 14](#/tournament/BotProLeague14) and turned pro. I remember thinking, oh no, this is real now, I'm going to have to wear a collared shirt for the photos.

**Turning pro didn't go smoothly at first. You went out in the first round of the [Audax Esse BPL Invitational 2026](#/tournament/audax-esse-bpl-invitational-2026) and in the group stage at [Bot Pro Cup](#/tournament/bot-pro-cup-2026). Were there doubts?**

Heaps. Anyone who tells you they didn't have doubts after that is lying to you. We lost a lot of maps in August and September, and my rating points were going down like a lift with the cable cut. But [Drew](#/player/88exp) kept saying the same thing every night: we're not far off, we're losing the close ones, keep the faith. Turns out he was right, which he will now remind me of until the sun burns out.

**You joined the BPL this year, which makes you part of the league's 6th Generation. Does it feel strange beating teams full of players who've been here since 2020?**

Nah, that's the best bit. The Founders built the place and I've got massive respect for them, but somebody's got to come in and start knocking things over. 6th Generation, first ever Nova Initia MVP. Put it on the badge. Actually, can you put it on the badge? Can we make it gold? *(laughs)* I'm only half joking. I'm about a quarter joking.

**Your share of the prize was $40,000, nearly five times what you'd won in your whole career before this event. Any big purchases?**

New chair. The old one squeaks every time I peek, which is a lot, so you can imagine. And I owe [Drew](#/player/88exp) a meal, because I promised him one if we made the final, and then I promised him another one if we won it. So that's two meals. He's going to order the most expensive thing on the menu twice. I can already see it. I've made my peace with it.

**[xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) are now 11th in the BPL ranking. What's next?**

Top ten, obviously. Eleventh is a rubbish number, nobody puts "11th" on a shirt. We've shown we can beat anyone on our day; now we've got to win when it isn't our day. Consistency. That's the boring answer. The fun answer is I want another MVP, at a bigger event, so I can have two of them sitting next to each other on the shelf and make my flatmate's life even worse.

**Last one. What would you say to whoever ends up MVP of the Nova Initia Invitational II?**

Congratulations, mate, genuinely. Enjoy it. Soak it all in, you've earned it. *(pauses)* Just remember you're the second one.

Cursiffe's Nova Initia numbers: 12 maps, 216 kills, 158 deaths, 35 MVP rounds and a 1.23 rating. He asked us to print all of them. We were happy to.

Going into the [[Nova Initia Invitational I]], [[Cursiffe]] was ranked 187th in the BPL. He came out of it with a trophy, a $40,000 payday, a climb of 125 places in the ranking and a line in the history books that can never be rewritten: the first MVP the event has ever had.

The Australian rifler finished the tournament with 216 kills, the most of anyone in the field and two more than his own teammate [[TokieShepherdVT]]. Across 12 maps he posted a 1.23 rating, the best at the event, a hair ahead of [[Artisian]]'s [[SanCtuary]] on 1.22 and [[TokieShepherdVT]] on 1.21. Along the way [[xPlosiv]] knocked out [[5PERCENT]], [[Artisian]] and [[Round Loss Bonus]], then beat [[Mourningstar]] 3-2 in a final that went the full five maps.

He is also, it turns out, extremely good company. We caught up with him to talk about the run, the triple overtime that nearly ended it, the Team Australia snub, and what it feels like to be the answer to a trivia question forever.

**Congratulations. A couple of weeks on, has it sunk in that you're the first MVP in Nova Initia history?**

Mate, I've been telling everyone. My flatmate is sick of it. I walk into the kitchen and go "morning, from the first ever Nova Initia MVP" and he just picks up his toast and leaves. *(laughs)* No, honestly, it's mental. There's going to be a Nova Initia II, a III, a Nova Initia X one day, and every single one of them gets an MVP. But there's only ever one first. They can't print a second first one. That one's mine, forever. Write that down. Actually, you are writing it down. Good.

**You didn't exactly start like an MVP. Eight kills on Vertigo against [[5PERCENT]], the lowest on your team.**

Oi, we won that map 13-1! There were fourteen rounds. What was I meant to do, run into their spawn and fight them in the doorway? *(laughs)* [[StrigidaeVT]] took 18 off them and wouldn't shut up about it for the rest of the day. The mood was "nobody expects anything, so let's have a crack". Best place to be. Everyone had us going home there, and I'd seen the odds. I screenshotted them, actually. For later. *(grins)*

Vertigo we nicked 13-11 and I had 21, felt unreal. Then on Mirage they smacked us 13-9 and [[SanCtuary]] was doing [[SanCtuary]] things. I had 19 on that map and it didn't matter one bit, which is the worst feeling in the game. Then Dust2.

**Dust2 went to triple overtime and finished 22-20. Take us inside that.**

Mate. I aged about ten years. Regulation ends 12-12, fine, we've all been to overtime. First overtime, 3-3. Second overtime, 3-3. At 18-18 [[88EXP]] goes quiet on comms for about five seconds, and when [[88EXP|Drew]] goes quiet you know he's cooking something. He calls a full commit onto A site we hadn't touched all half, and it just works. Four rounds later we're through and I'm screaming into my mic like a galah.

I finished that map with 31 kills. People keep bringing up the 31. I would like people to keep bringing up the 31. Please, everyone reading this, keep bringing up the 31.

**[[SanCtuary]] finished the event on a 1.22, one hundredth behind you. Were you watching his numbers?**

Course I was. I'm not going to sit here and pretend I wasn't refreshing the stats page between maps. *(laughs)* Look, [[SanCtuary]] is a monster. He did that in six maps and I needed twelve, so you can make whatever argument you like down the pub. But the rule's the rule, and the rule says one point two three beats one point two two. Maths is maths. If he wants an MVP he can come and win the second one at Nova II. I'll leave the door open for him. Slightly. Just a smidge.

**The semifinal against [[Round Loss Bonus]] was a 2-0, and Inferno might have been your best map of the event: 21 kills, 13 deaths and six MVP rounds.**

That one's going on the fridge. Inferno is a map where if you win your duels, you win the round, and I was winning all of them. Six MVP rounds on one map. I rang my mum. She didn't know what an MVP round was, but she was very proud. Then we won Dust2 13-1 and [[tapiyokaaa]] said "maybe we should save a few rounds for the final", and I said "mate, it doesn't work like that". It doesn't. I checked.

**The final. [[Mourningstar]] won the opener on Inferno 13-6, and you were still [[xPlosiv|xPlosiv's]] top fragger with 18 kills. What was said after that map?**

Honestly? Nothing, for about a minute. Then [[TokieShepherdVT|Tokie]] unmuted and said "right, my turn", and went and dropped 26 on Tuscan. That's just [[TokieShepherdVT|Tokie]]. She doesn't do speeches, she does damage. We won Tuscan 13-9, then Anubis 13-1, and I'm sitting there thinking, sweet as, we're cruising, I'll start practising my trophy face.

**And then Dust2 happened.**

Yeah. Don't. *(laughs)* 21 kills, eight assists, and we lose 13-10. Eight assists! The one time in my life I play like a team player, and look where it gets me. Credit to [[Mourningstar]] though, they'd come up through [[Bot Pro Cup 2026]] and nobody gave them a chance either. They played like a team with nothing to lose, because they had nothing to lose. And [[EXaCT]] was everywhere. She finished the event four kills behind me, by the way. I know because I checked. Twice.

**Mirage, map five. You won it 13-3. How does a final that close end that lopsided?**

Because we'd already been to triple overtime against [[Artisian]], mate. Nothing scares you after that. [[88EXP|Drew]] called it slow and patient, we took map control round after round, and they started forcing. I had 15 kills and six deaths, [[StrigidaeVT|Strigi]] had 18, [[tapiyokaaa]] had six MVP rounds. Everyone turned up at once. When the last round went in I stood up so fast I knocked my headset off the desk. It's got a crack in it now. I'm keeping it like that.

**[[xPlosiv]] won an S-Tier without a dedicated AWPer. How does that work, and what's your job in it?**

Five rifles, no excuses. *(grins)* Everyone asks us who our AWPer is and we just say "yes". The idea's dead simple: if all five of us can win a rifle duel, the other team never gets a free pick on us.[[88EXP|Drew]] calls it, [[TokieShepherdVT|Tokie]] and [[tapiyokaaa]] are the big guns, [[StrigidaeVT|Strigi]] does all the dirty work nobody ever notices, and my job is to be the bloke who walks into the room first and makes it everyone else's problem. I'm also the loud one. Somebody has to be.

Little bit. I won't lie to you. You want to wear the green and gold. The lads who got picked, [[gigichiii_]] and that crew, they deserve it, they're absolute class. But me and [[88EXP|Drew]] had a chat after that semi, and the vibe was "righto, we'll just have to go and win something bigger then". Eight days later we're holding an S-Tier trophy. I'm not saying the selectors got it wrong. I'm just saying they might want to check their emails.

**Let's go back to the start. Your first BPL event was [[Bot Pro Minor League 13]] in May, and [[xPlosiv]] finished tenth. What changed?**

Pretty much everything except me and [[TokieShepherdVT|Tokie]]. That first lineup was good people, but it wasn't clicking. articles.title: xPlosiv win the inaugural Nova Initia Invitational
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
The league has a shiny new event on its calendar, and it could hardly have asked for a better debut. The Nova Initia Invitational I, a fresh S-Tier tournament, delivered drama from the opening round to a five-map final, and when the dust settled it was [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) lifting the very first trophy in the competition's history.

Nobody would have called them favourites. [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) came in as an unfancied name, and they do it the hard way, fielding an all-rifle lineup with no dedicated AWPer at all. In an era of specialists, they simply out-gunned people, and it worked from the very first match.

Their bracket run was a steady build toward a crescendo. A comfortable 2-0 over [5PERCENT](#/team/5percent) opened proceedings, before a 2-1 over the S-Tier winners [Artisian](#/team/artisian) announced that this was no fluke. A 2-0 dismissal of [Round Loss Bonus](#/team/round-loss-bonus) in the semifinal booked their place in the final, and set up a title match nobody saw coming.

Because waiting in that final was one of the stories of the season. [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar), freshly promoted to pro out of Bot Pro Cup, had kept their cinderella run going all the way to an S-Tier final. Their reward was a shot at the trophy, and they made [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) earn every inch of it.

The final was a classic. Across a full five maps, [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) refused to fold, dragging the champions to the brink before [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv) finally closed it out 3-2. It was the kind of match that makes a new event's name, and both teams walked away with their reputations enhanced, even if only one of them got the silverware.

The engine of it all was xPlosiv's rifle core. [TokieShepherdVT](#/player/tokieshepherdvt) led the charge up top, with [tapiyokaaa](#/player/tapiyokaaa) and [Cursiffe](#/player/cursiffe) providing relentless support and [88EXP](#/player/88exp) steering the team from the caller's chair alongside [StrigidaeVT](#/player/strigidaevt). No AWP, no problem. They pointed five rifles downrange and refused to lose the duel.

In the third-place match, [Round Loss Bonus](#/team/round-loss-bonus) edged [Nightshade](#/team/nightshade) 13-8 to round out the podium. But the day belonged to [xPlosiv](#/team/xplosiv), who have surged up the rankings on the back of their maiden S-Tier title. A new tournament has a first champion, and it is a name few expected to be reading. Not a bad way to start a legacy.

articles.title: Opal defy the odds to win Bot Pro Cup 2026
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
Forget the predictions. Forget the seedings. Forget everything the group stage told us, because [Opal](#/team/opal) have just authored one of the great fairytales in Bot Pro Cup history, storming through the playoff bracket to be crowned champions of Bot Pro Cup 2026. Nobody had them here. They did it anyway.

The run was nothing short of ruthless. In the round of sixteen, [Opal](#/team/opal) drew the tournament's most feared floater, the talent-stacked [division20](#/team/division20), and dispatched them 2-0 without blinking. A 2-0 over [Solstice](#/team/solstice) followed in the quarterfinals, and suddenly the team nobody was talking about was ninety minutes from a trophy.

Then came the moment that will define this tournament. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) had been the story of the season, a machine riding a nine-match win streak, the longest tear anyone had been on in years and the closest thing the league had seen to threatening the all-time record of thirteen straight set by [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch)'s dynasty. Cosmos looked unstoppable. [Opal](#/team/opal) stopped them. A clinical 2-0 in the semifinal ended the streak stone dead, denied Cosmos their shot at history, and kept the dynasty's record firmly intact. If you wanted a statement, that was it.

The final was almost a formality by comparison, though the opponent was anything but ordinary. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), the breakout newcomers and the cinderella darlings of the whole event, stood between Opal and the title. It did not matter. [Opal](#/team/opal) closed it out 3-1, turning the dream final into a coronation and sending the fairytale newcomers home as runners-up.

What makes this special is who [Opal](#/team/opal) are, or rather who they used to be. Three years ago they were a genuine contender, a team good enough to win almost anything, forever running into the one obstacle nobody in that era could clear: [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) and their dynasty. When that door stayed shut, Opal faded, and for three long years they were an afterthought, a name from a bygone age.

Now, out of nowhere, they are reborn. This is not a fluke run by a plucky underdog. This is a former powerhouse rediscovering its best form at exactly the right moment, and doing it in devastating fashion. The core did the damage, with [lumi.nyaa](#/player/lumi-nyaa) leading the fragging, [joyyy_cheng](#/player/joyyy-cheng) marshalling the team from the caller's chair, and [kuro_mi](#/player/kuro-mi) chipping in alongside the double-AWP look of [Seireiix](#/player/seireiix) and [Scorpium](#/player/scorpium). They did not just win. They looked like a team that belongs at the very top.

The numbers back it up. [Opal](#/team/opal) have surged up the rankings on the back of an eight-match winning streak of their own, and for the first time in three years they look every bit the contender they once were. The dark horses were tamed, the streak was broken, and the newcomers were denied. This was Opal's day, and on this evidence, it may be the first of many. The old guard is back.

articles.title: Bot Pro Cup 2026: the group stage delivers chaos, and the playoffs await
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
The group stage of Bot Pro Cup 2026 is finally in the books, and what a ride it was. Eight groups, dozens of teams, and weeks of ruthless Swiss-format chaos have finally spat out the sixteen survivors who advance to the playoffs. Some of them were always going to be here. Plenty of them were not supposed to be, and that is exactly what made this group stage one of the most gripping stretches of Counter-Strike the league has served up in a long time.

Let us start with the perfect runs, because there were two of them. [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) tore through Group B without dropping a match, a clean 5-0 that reminded everyone why they sit among the very best teams in the league. Led by the firepower of [sneakyyyyy](#/player/sneakyyyyy), they looked a class above their group and enter the bracket as the team to beat. But they were not alone in running the table. [Wraithborne](#/team/wraithborne), a North American newcomer nobody outside their own Discord was talking about a month ago, went 5-0 in Group G and did it against real competition. From unknown quantity to undefeated group winner and freshly minted pro team, their rise has been the story of the tournament.

And Wraithborne are not even close to alone in that fairytale. Seven amateur teams punched their ticket to the playoffs and, with it, earned pro status. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), [Nightshade](#/team/nightshade), [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar), [Syzygy](#/team/syzygy), [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence), [Solstice](#/team/solstice) and [Wraithborne](#/team/wraithborne) all walked in as hopefuls and walked out as professional organisations. Every one of them has a story. [Syzygy](#/team/syzygy) finally delivering on [Xyrren](#/player/xyrren)'s long-held dream of a pro team. [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide) topping their group behind the ice-cold [Codiant](#/player/codiant). [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) carrying the reborn ex-Astral Bloom trio back to the top table. These are the runs that make a cup worth running.

The bubble was where hearts got broken. Several groups came down to the final round, and the teams that squeezed through in second on a 3-2 record all had to survive a scare or two to do it. [Mourningstar](#/team/mourningstar) edged Group C, [Artisian](#/team/artisian) held their nerve in Group E, and [Kiedz](#/team/kiedz) escaped a brutal Group H behind the elite AWPing of [Elfy Mint](#/player/elfy-mint). For every cinderella story that ends with a promotion, there is a favourite left staring at the exit wondering how a Swiss run got away from them, and this group stage had plenty of those too.

Of course, the established powers mostly did what established powers do. Alongside [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos), the S-Tier winners [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) and [Artisian](#/team/artisian) navigated through, as did a strong [Opal](#/team/opal) team and the ever-dangerous [Sacred Raven](#/team/sacred-raven) and [Moonlit Tempo](#/team/moonlit-tempo). [Flood Flashers](#/team/flood-flashers) backed up their pedigree with a second-place finish in the brutal Group A. These are teams with the experience and the ceiling to win the whole thing, and none of them will fear the bracket.

And yet for every giant that held serve, another fell flat on its face. This is where Bot Pro Cup 2026 turned genuinely brutal, because the group stage did not just produce cinderellas, it produced carnage among the household names. Six of the league's top ten teams failed to reach the playoffs, and the list reads like a hall of fame gone wrong. Pedigree, it turns out, counts for nothing if you do not show up.

The most staggering casualty of them all is [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch). The number one team in the league, the dynasty, the most decorated roster the scene has ever produced, went 1-3 in Group A and finished seventh of nine. Read that again. If you had offered anyone that result before the tournament, they would have laughed you out of the room. [New Jade](#/team/new-jade), a top-five team, somehow did worse, finishing dead last in Group C without a single meaningful win to show for it. It was the kind of collapse that ends seasons and starts hard conversations.

They had plenty of company. [Neverland](#/team/neverland) and [Lemon Tree](#/team/lemon-tree) both stumbled to 2-3 records and out, unable to string together the wins their rankings demanded. [entity](#/team/entity) went 2-2 in a nightmarish Group A and joined Aimpunch among the fallen. And spare a thought for [Infernum E-Sports](#/team/infernum-e-sports), who did just about everything right, posted a winning 3-2 record, and still missed out on a tiebreaker heartbreaker, the cruelest way to bow out of any Swiss stage. For a clutch of teams that were supposed to be circling the trophy, the group stage was a reckoning.

But if you are looking for the team nobody wants to draw, look at [division20](#/team/division20). On paper they carry the most talent of any qualifier, anchored by [Laburi](#/player/laburi), the highest-rated player in the entire league. For a season now they have been the great underachievers, a super-team that could not translate individual brilliance into results. They qualified 4-1 from Group C, and if they have finally found their rhythm at the right moment, they are a genuine wrecking ball waiting to happen. Nobody sensible is booking a match against Laburi and friends.

So here we are. Sixteen teams, single elimination, four rounds, one trophy. The bracket is a beautiful collision of grizzled contenders and wide-eyed newcomers, of teams playing for legacy and teams playing for the simple joy of having made it this far. There is going to be an upset. There is going to be a run that nobody predicts. And somewhere in these sixteen names is a champion who will look back on this cup as the moment everything changed.

Time for the part where the BPL staff put their neck on the line. On the numbers, [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) are the clear favourites. They are the highest-ranked team in the field, they own a Major title, they were the most convincing team in the group stage, and their roster average sits near the top of the qualifiers. If you forced us to bet the house on one name, it would be theirs. Right behind them, [The Gigarage](#/team/the-gigarage) and [Artisian](#/team/artisian) have the trophies and the depth to go all the way, and either would be a worthy winner.

The dark horse, though, is [division20](#/team/division20). No qualifier has a higher roster rating, and talent like that does not stay quiet forever. Our bold shout is that this is the tournament where they finally click, and a [division20](#/team/division20) versus [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) final would be a fitting climax between the team with the most silverware potential and the team with the most raw firepower. And keep half an eye on [Prism Divide](#/team/prism-divide), the strongest of the newcomers on paper, because cinderella does not always turn back into a pumpkin at midnight.

Prediction locked in: [Cosmos](#/team/cosmos) to lift the trophy, with [division20](#/team/division20) the dark horse most likely to ruin the script. But predictions are made to be broken, and that is exactly why we cannot wait for the first map to go live. The group stage gave us chaos, heartbreak and seven new pro teams. If the playoffs give us even half as much drama, we are all in for a treat. Bring on the bracket.

articles.title: miorine erupts for 22-6 on rifle debut against Aeternum
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
Well, that answers that. Barely a week after [miorine](#/player/miorine) put down the AWP to move onto the rifle, he made his debut in the new role, and it could hardly have gone better. Facing [Aeternum](#/team/aeternum) at Bot Pro Cup 2026, he exploded for a jaw-dropping 22 kills to just 6 deaths, dragging [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) to a comfortable 13-5 win on Dust2.

A 22-6 line is a statement in any game, let alone a first outing in an unfamiliar role. That is a 3.67 K/D, topped off with 4 MVP rounds, the kind of performance that turns heads and quiets doubters in a single map. Whatever nerves might come with reinventing yourself mid-season, [miorine](#/player/miorine) clearly left them at the door.

It is exactly the sort of debut the switch was gambling on. Freed from the lonely responsibility of the AWP, [miorine](#/player/miorine) looked fast, aggressive and completely at home with a rifle in hand, taking space and winning duels all over the map. On this evidence, the move looks less like a risk and more like a player finally being handed the tools that suit him.

For [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) the timing could not be better. With [heavenweeps](#/player/heavenweeps) settled as the team's sole sniper and [miorine](#/player/miorine) firing alongside [Decrease](#/player/decrease) in the rifle line, in front of [Soozy](#/player/soozy) and [Ziweiv](#/player/ziweiv), the new structure delivered immediately. One game is a small sample, but as first impressions go, this one was emphatic.

There will be tougher tests ahead, and one blowout does not make a season. Still, if [miorine](#/player/miorine) can bottle even a fraction of this, [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) may have stumbled onto something special. The AWP era is over, and the rifle era has started with a bang.

articles.title: Lunar Cadence reach the playoffs as the Astral Bloom trio climb back to pro
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
[Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) have booked their place in the Bot Pro Cup 2026 playoffs and, with it, earned pro status. It is a milestone for the whole roster, but it carries a special weight for three players in particular, because this is a redemption story as much as a promotion.

Not long ago, [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami), [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) and [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) were shipped out of [Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom) in a three-for-three trade, cast as part of the problem on a team stuck at the bottom of the standings. Rather than fade away, the trio regrouped at [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence), put their heads down, and ground their way back up through the Bot Pro Cup. Now they are pro again, and they did it the hard way.

Around them, [Lunar Cadence](#/team/lunar-cadence) have built a tidy unit. [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) anchors the AWP, [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami) and [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) lead the rifle line, and they are joined by in-game leader [briant](#/player/briant) and the young [Tatsumaki Chise](#/player/tatsumaki-chise). It is a lineup that clearly clicked when it mattered most.

And here is where it gets interesting. [Astral Bloom](#/team/astral-bloom), who kept [Remia Aotsuki](#/player/remia-aotsuki) and [Tachibana Hinano](#/player/tachibana-hinano) as their core and traded the trio away, are still languishing near the foot of the table on a 7-18 map record. The three players they moved on from just qualified for a pro playoff. It raises an uncomfortable question for the org: what if the problem was never the players who left?

It would be too easy to call it right now. The sample is small, the playoffs are still to come, and one good run does not rewrite a career. But the early evidence is hard to ignore. [Eris Suzukami](#/player/eris-suzukami), [Tsumugi Kokage](#/player/tsumugi-kokage) and [Shiranami Ramune](#/player/shiranami-ramune) have answered their doubters in the most direct way possible, and the rest of the story will write itself. That is to be seen.

articles.title: miorine puts down the AWP to rifle for Cyanide
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
[Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) are shaking up their setup, with [miorine](#/player/miorine) set to put down the AWP and move into a full-time rifling role. After a long stint behind the big green rifle, the Singaporean is trading the sniper's patience for the pace of the entry, and it marks one of the more intriguing personal reinventions of the season.

The switch reshapes the way [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) attack. With [miorine](#/player/miorine) stepping off the AWP, sole sniper duties now fall to [heavenweeps](#/player/heavenweeps), while [miorine](#/player/miorine) joins [Decrease](#/player/decrease) to form a beefed-up rifle line in front of in-game leader [Soozy](#/player/soozy) and the versatile [Ziweiv](#/player/ziweiv). It is a cleaner division of labour, with one dedicated AWPer and a heavier rifle presence.

For [miorine](#/player/miorine) it is a chance to reset. The AWP is the most punishing role in the game, and his numbers there had dipped over the season. A move to rifle lets him play faster, take more space, and lean on aim and timing rather than the lonely responsibility of holding an angle with the most expensive weapon on the server.

Role changes like this are never guaranteed to click, but they can unlock a player who was quietly miscast. If [miorine](#/player/miorine) settles quickly, [Cyanide](#/team/cyanide) come away with a more aggressive rifle core and a tidier structure. If not, it is a low-risk experiment for a team looking for any edge it can find.

Either way, it is a bold call to walk away from a role you have played for years. [miorine](#/player/miorine) is betting that his best rounds are still ahead of him, just with a different weapon in hand.

articles.title: Free agency over already: mond33__ lands at Feral Instinct
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
If you blinked, you missed her free agency. Barely hours after the bombshell of [mond33__](#/player/mond33) parting ways with [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch), the six-time champion already has a new home. Feral Instinct have moved fast to sign the veteran AWPer, and just like that, one of the shortest spells on the open market in recent memory is over.

It is a statement of intent from an ambitious amateur team. Feral Instinct release AWPer [Loonatic](#/player/loonatic), who becomes a free agent, and hand the sniper role to a player with more big-match pedigree than the entire amateur scene combined. This is a straight upgrade in the seat, and more than that, it is a gamble on everything a champion carries beyond raw numbers.

Because make no mistake, this is a gamble. [mond33__](#/player/mond33) arrives off the dip in form that cost her the Aimpunch seat, and nobody is pretending her fragging is what it once was. But Feral Instinct are not buying this season's stat line. They are buying six titles of composure, a decade of knowing exactly what to do when a round is on the line, and a veteran presence that a rising team simply cannot teach.

The fit is a good one. She slots in alongside the firepower of [MKakili](#/player/mkakili) and [wushii](#/player/wushii), with [qebo](#/player/qebo) calling and [TRPaki](#/player/trpaki) rounding out the lineup, and suddenly a team that was searching for an edge has a genuine leader on the roster. If her experience rubs off even a little, Feral Instinct become a very different proposition.

For [mond33__](#/player/mond33) herself, it is a fresh chapter and a fascinating one. She goes from the summit of the pro scene to leading a promotion charge from the amateur ranks, with a point to prove to a team that decided it no longer needed her. Legends do not fade quietly, and a champion with something to prove is exactly the kind of player who drags a team upward. This one is going to be worth watching.

articles.title: SHOCK exit: mond33__ parts ways with Aimpunch after years of greatness
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
WOAH. In a move that has sent shockwaves through the entire Bot Pro League, [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) and their legendary AWPer [mond33__](#/player/mond33) are parting ways. Read that again. One of the most decorated players in the history of the league, a cornerstone of the greatest dynasty the scene has ever seen, has suddenly been cut loose and is a free agent. Nobody saw this coming.

Make no mistake about how big this is. [mond33__](#/player/mond33) is one of only three players tied for the most event titles in league history, level with [Sketch](#/player/sketch) at the very summit. She was there for every single triumph, the sniper behind years of trophies, and [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) touching their championship core is almost unthinkable. This is the end of an era, plain and simple.

So why break up greatness? Because [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) do not do sentiment. Over recent play [mond33__](#/player/mond33) had quietly become the roster's least productive fragger in the duel, and a team that refuses to settle for anything less than the top made the coldest call in the book. If it can happen to a six-time champion, it can happen to anyone. That is the ruthless standard that built the dynasty in the first place.

Into the vacated AWP seat steps [Aranionja](#/player/aranionja), and she arrives with a point to prove. A Singaporean sniper with a big, proven sample and a title already to her name, she walks away from a stacked but unranked Rebellium for the chance of a lifetime. It is a pure glory move, trading a talented team still waiting for its breakthrough for the most successful team the league has ever produced. On the numbers, she is a clear upgrade in the seat.

Rebellium did not sit still either. They already run a second AWPer in [Tosaki Mimi](#/player/tosaki-mimi), and they moved fast to sign free agent [estellyy.](#/player/estellyy), recently let go by Masmark, to fill the gap. She is a proven Singaporean sniper who slots straight in beside the elite firepower of [rebebx](#/player/rebebx), and her spell on the open market proved mercifully short.

But the story of the day is [mond33__](#/player/mond33). A six-time champion, a dynasty icon, is somehow available, and the phones will not stop ringing. [Aimpunch](#/team/aimpunch) have reloaded and served notice that even a team with nothing left to prove will never stop hunting for an edge. Ruthless, stunning, and completely unforgettable. This is a day the league will be talking about for a long time.

articles.title: Solec, the original king of the rifle
articles.author: BPL Staff
articles.body:
Long before [Laburi](#/player/laburi) sat atop the rating charts, and before [rebebx](#/player/rebebx) made his own case for the crown, there was [Solec](#/player/solec). Ask anyone who was around in the early years and the answer comes back the same: he was the greatest to ever touch a rifle in the Bot Pro League. The trouble is that the numbers will never prove it, and that is the strange, quiet tragedy at the heart of his legacy.

From 2021 to early 2024, [Solec](#/player/solec) was the tip of the spear for [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer). He was an entry fragger in the purest sense, the man who opened sites on his own, taking the first duel so his teammates could pour in behind him. It was a brutal, thankless role, and he made it look like art. Hints of that peak still flicker through the old games, a reminder of just how far ahead of his time he was.

Here is the catch. The league did not track detailed statistics during the years [Solec](#/player/solec) was at his devastating best, so there is no leaderboard to enshrine him, no rating line to point to. Those who watched know what they saw. Had the numbers been recorded, a player of his calibre would sit comfortably above a 1.25 K/D across his enormous 130-map history. The evidence lives in memory rather than in a spreadsheet, which is exactly why his story is worth telling.

In time, the fragging star followed a path much like [Sketch](#/player/sketch)'s. As he tells it himself, he began to get inconsistent, the razor edge that defined his entry play starting to dull. Rather than cling to a role that was slipping, he leaned on his extensive history in the league and moved into the in-game leader's chair, trading the first bullet for the first word.

The reinvention has been a success on its own terms. [Solec](#/player/solec) now wins rounds with his mind, his calls carving open rounds the way his rifle once did, and he has passed the torch cleanly. His successor as the tip of the spear, [LITA](#/player/lita), has been doing outstanding work on the server, the new engine to Solec's steady hand at the wheel.

For all his brilliance, the one prize has always slipped away. [Divide&Conquer](#/team/divide-conquer) are specialists in the upset, a Minor League winner and a team that has reached the biggest stages, most agonisingly the Audax Esse 2025 final, only to fall at the last step. The heartbreak of that run could have broken a lesser team. Instead it lit a fire.

They are hungry now, driven toward a title in 2026 with a passion that refuses to fade. [Solec](#/player/solec) put it best in his own words: maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not for a long while, but one day, I will win a major. Whether or not that day comes, his place is already secure. Before the charts, before the numbers, before the names everyone now knows, there was Solec, the original king of the rifle.
